title: Tap-Drill Numeric Verification

primary_source_obtained.access_method: Authorized standards-reseller preview page (standards.iteh.ai sample PDF, linked from their public catalogue listing for ISO 2306:1972), not a paywall bypass — this is the same kind of pre-purchase preview a reseller routinely publishes.
primary_source_obtained.content_obtained: Full 8-page standard: scope, Table 1 (ISO metric coarse pitch), Table 2 (ISO metric fine pitch), Table 3 (UNC), Table 4 (UNF), Table 5/6 (pipe threads), Table 7 (metric summary annex).
primary_source_obtained.copyright_note: Table values (bare numbers) were read and used to cross-check BoltLab's existing data. No standard text, table formatting, or substantial content was reproduced into BoltLab's repository — only the resulting comparison/verification outcome and the specific numeric drill diameters already present in BoltLab's own datasets.

conflict_type: different_standard — US customary inch drill-series convention (BoltLab's existing unc/unf datasets) vs. ISO 2306:1972's continuous-metric-drill-diameter convention for the same inch thread sizes

value_meaning_distinctions_captured.metric: BoltLab's tap_drill_mm values are now confirmed to be ISO 2306 Table 1's own basic/theoretical recommended drill diameter (nominal minus pitch, mapped to the ISO/R 235 stocked drill series) — not a percentage-of-thread-engagement value, not a manufacturer recommendation, not a finished-hole measurement.
value_meaning_distinctions_captured.unc_unf_existing: BoltLab's tap_drill_in values remain of unconfirmed origin (T1 described them only as 'Public engineering reference synthesis'); they were NOT shown in this phase to derive from ISO 2306, and do not exactly match it. Their actual source convention (likely a customary-drill-series, percentage-engagement-target chart) was not independently re-derived in T2.1.
value_meaning_distinctions_captured.unc_unf_iso_2306: ISO 2306's inch-thread values are metric drill diameters recommended for tapping the same inch thread, derived by ISO's own approximation rule — a legitimate but distinct engineering recommendation from BoltLab's existing values, not a correction to them.

scope_boundary_note: Expanding unc.seed.json/unf.seed.json to cover the 9 UNC/UNF sizes with no existing BoltLab base-thread record (#4-40, #6-32, #8-32, #10-24, 1/2-13, #6-40, #8-36, #10-32, 1/2-20) was NOT performed in this phase. This would mean adding new records to a pre-existing, previously-verified, non-tapping-domain dataset — a larger scope decision flagged for explicit approval rather than executed unilaterally. The ISO 2306 values for these 9 sizes are captured above so this research is not lost.
